The Spurs' young core continued to shine in their overtime victory against Utah, with Victor Wembanyama and Jeremy Vassell leading the charge. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson acknowledged the difficulty of winning in the NBA, saying it's hard to win regardless of circumstances. He praised his team for their resilience and determination, giving them credit for turning the game around after a slow start. Wembanyama and Vassell were instrumental in securing the win, scoring four points each in the extra frame. Vassell's impressive dunk after Dylan Harper's shot was blocked at the rim gave the Spurs a 111-108 lead before Wembanyama pushed it to a seven-point cushion with a 13-foot jumper. The Jazz put up a tough fight, but ultimately fell short as the Spurs' young core proved too strong. The win is a testament to the team's growing chemistry and determination, and they will look to build on this momentum in their next game. The San Antonio Spurs' offense was firing on all cylinders as all five starters managed to score in double figures against the Utah Jazz. This impressive display helped the team overcome an 11-point deficit in the second period, demonstrating their resilience and ability to bounce back from adversity. Keyonte George led the Jazz with a game-high 31 points, but it wasn't enough to secure a win for his team. Other notable contributors for Utah included Ace Bailey's 19 points and rookie Darryn Peterson's 18 points. The Spurs' victory was sealed in overtime after Brice Sensabaugh and George each hit crucial shots to send the game into extra time. Victor Wembanyama shone brightly for the Spurs, delivering his best performance of the season with an impressive 30-point outing. He also racked up five assists, two steals, and two blocks in 39 minutes on court, showcasing his versatility and skill. Devin Vassell played a pivotal role in the team's overtime victory against Utah, earning praise from his teammates for his clutch performance. Vassell's contribution was particularly notable after halftime, as he scored 17 of his 21 points to provide crucial support to Victor Wembanyama. His efforts helped shift the momentum in favor of the Spurs, who had been struggling to find their footing at the start of the season. articles.title: Liverpool Defeat Chelsea in Penalty Shootout Again
articles.summary: The Reds won against Chelsea for the fifth consecutive time in a penalty shootout.
articles.content: Liverpool's history with penalties against Chelsea is well-documented, and Xabi Alonso knows it all too well from his playing days at Anfield. Alonso, who won several trophies for Liverpool on spot kicks, witnessed a familiar scenario unfold as he watched the Reds defeat Chelsea in a shootout. This was not an isolated incident; the two teams have a history of engaging in penalty shootouts against each other, with Chelsea emerging on the losing side every time. This trend began in 2007 during the Champions League semi-finals, when Alonso scored for Liverpool in their 1-0 win over Chelsea. Since then, Chelsea has participated in four more shootouts against Liverpool, all of which they lost. Chelsea's penalty woes continued last night as they failed to capitalize on spot kicks in both halves of the game. Alonso noted that reaching penalties often spells disaster for his former opponents, and it was no different this time around. The final nail in Chelsea's coffin came when Wesley Fofana shot high into the Kop, securing Liverpool's fifth consecutive shootout victory over Chelsea. Chelsea's quest for silverware has taken a hit, as they were eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Liverpool for the third time in six seasons. This latest setback is particularly frustrating for Xabi Alonso, who had been eyeing his first chance at winning a domestic trophy since Chelsea's last cup victory in 2018. Liverpool, on the other hand, are taking an unconventional route to their third Carabao Cup title in six seasons. After navigating through tough matches against Spurs and Chelsea, they now face another challenging opponent in the quarter-finals - Bournemouth, whose manager Iraola has a history with. Alonso, however, would have preferred a different draw. The decisive spot kick that sealed Liverpool's victory was converted by Joe Gomez, who surprisingly scored his first goal at Anfield after 278 games and 12 seasons. The fact that several substitutes, including Alexis Mac Allister, Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo, Florian Wirtz, and Bradley Barcola, found the net from 12 yards suggests that Iraola's strategy of holding back key players may have paid off. Iraola himself expressed his delight at seeing his team come through in a tough situation, saying "When I have done the last subs and I put Alexis and Alex on, it starts to be in your head." His words reflect the confidence and composure that Liverpool displayed throughout the match. The penalty shootout continued to be a nightmare for Chelsea as Kostas Tsimikas's shot sailed wide of the post after Valentin Barco hit the woodwork earlier in the sequence. In the first 12 penalties, there had been no saves made by either goalkeeper, but Mike Penders and Giorgi Mamardashvili broke this streak with two crucial parries, one each from Ryan Gravenberch's effort and Emmanuel Emegha's debut penalty attempt. Morgan Rogers's well-taken spot kick gave Chelsea a lead after Cody Gakpo had levelled the game with his own penalty conversion, both goals coming from 12 yards as the teams traded penalties in quick succession. The only other goals of regulation time were scored from penalty spots, with Gravenberch and Rogers scoring for their respective teams after a series of careless fouls. The game hung in the balance after regulation time, with both teams still level. Liverpool goalkeeper Penders made a crucial save on Ronald Araujo's header, denying the Barcelona defender what could have been a winning goal. Penders also thwarted Barcola's attempt to break the deadlock, showcasing his impressive reflexes and composure under pressure. Alonso praised Penders' performance, describing it as "really solid". The Chelsea goalkeeper made another crucial intervention during the penalty shootout, saving Ryan Gravenberch's spot kick. The only other goals of regulation time were scored from penalty spots, with Gravenberch and Rogers scoring for their respective teams after a series of careless fouls. Chelsea's summer signing Marco Palestra had an opportunity to open his account when he was supplied by Rogers, but Mamardashvili denied him in a one-on-one situation. The scoreline at the end of 90 minutes was probably fair, with both teams cancelling each other out and creating few clear-cut chances. The deployment of Henderson in an advanced role as a No 10 was a tactical surprise that added to the intrigue of the match. He seemed to be playing in place of Palmer, who is normally used in this position but was suspended for the game. On the other side, Liverpool's James McConnell took on a holding midfield role, providing defensive cover behind their lone striker. With Chelsea lacking creativity due to injuries and suspensions, it was no surprise that chances were scarce throughout the match. In the end, it was Liverpool who emerged victorious in the shootout, with each of their three big-name substitutes scoring against Chelsea's goalkeepers. articles.title: North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles off east coast
articles.summary: South Korea's defence ministry reports that North Korea has launched around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles, which were detected heading towards the East Sea before being tracked by South Korean and US military surveillance.
articles.content: North Korea has fired a significant number of short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast, according to Seoul's defence ministry. The exact number is around a dozen, but more details are still being analyzed by South Korean and US military officials. This latest launch comes on the heels of a series of recent weapons tests conducted by Pyongyang. In recent weeks, North Korea has demonstrated new capabilities with the deployment of advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence in its missile systems. The missiles were detected heading towards the East Sea, also known as the Sea of Japan, and flew approximately 250 kilometres before being tracked by South Korean and US military surveillance. The launches have prompted a heightened sense of vigilance among regional authorities, including the Japan Coast Guard which has issued warnings to ships in the area. The recent spate of missile launches by North Korea has sparked concerns about escalating tensions in the region. The launches have been widely condemned, with Seoul's National Security Office labeling them as "serious acts that do nothing to help manage the current situation". This assessment is based on the fact that the launches violate UN Security Council resolutions. The timing of these launches is particularly noteworthy, coming as they do against the backdrop of growing tensions over a landmine explosion along the heavily fortified border between North and South Korea. Three South Korean soldiers were wounded in this incident, which has heightened concerns about the safety of troops stationed on both sides of the border. A joint investigation by Seoul and the UN concluded that the landmines had been planted by North Korea over a year ago. The landmine explosion has led to accusations from Seoul that Pyongyang is engaging in provocative behavior. The South Korean government has demanded an apology for what it sees as a clear violation of the Armistice Agreement, but so far, this demand has been met with scorn from North Korea. This latest development has added to the already strained atmosphere between the two nations. The recent missile launches are also being seen as a demonstration of North Korea's military capabilities. According to Professor Lim Eul-chul of Kyungnam University, these launches show that Pyongyang is capable of causing significant damage to major South Korean and US military facilities. This assessment suggests that North Korea is sending a strong message about its military power and warning Seoul not to interfere with its efforts to fortify the border. The escalating tensions between North and South Korea have led to a series of provocative actions from Pyongyang, including the recent launch of around a dozen ballistic missiles. Both sides have employed psychological warfare methods in the past, such as using loudspeakers to broadcast propaganda across their shared border. In response to this latest escalation, South Korea proposed military talks with the North to confirm the precise location of their border and discuss restoring communication channels. The Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) is one of the world's most heavily fortified frontiers, a stark reminder of the ongoing tensions between the two nations. The Korean conflict may have ended in 1953 with a truce rather than a peace treaty, but Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war. As Washington weighs its options for potential nuclear talks with North Korea, concerns are growing that Seoul could be sidelined in favor of direct negotiations between the US and Pyongyang. articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers Win First World Series Championship
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers secured their first World Series championship, with ace pitcher Jacob Misiorowski playing a crucial role in the win.
articles.content: The Milwaukee Brewers have taken home their first World Series championship, and ace pitcher Jacob Misiorowski was instrumental in securing the win. In Game 5 of the series, the team opted to start their ace on regular rest, a strategic move that paid off as they took the field with the best possible lineup. Misiorowski's performance was crucial in this game, but it wasn't without some uncertainty. His playoff outings hadn't matched the dominance he showed during the regular season, and he had struggled to go beyond five innings in each start. However, when it mattered most, Misiorowski stepped up and delivered a strong outing. The Brewers' ace pitched 5 ⅔ scoreless innings, allowing just two hits as the team built a commanding lead. He was forced to leave the game late in the sixth inning due to a calf cramp, but the damage had already been done, and the team's elite bullpen took over with ease. Misiorowski's performance marked an impressive achievement, joining only one other pitcher in history who has recorded a scoreless start of 5+ innings with two or fewer hits allowed in a potential World Series clincher - Tom Glavine in 1995. The Brewers' World Series victory marked a remarkable achievement for their team and city, and pitcher Jacob Misiorowski played a crucial role in securing the championship. On the field after the clinching game, Misiorowski expressed his excitement and pride in the team's accomplishment, stating that it was "awesome" for both the team and the city of Milwaukee. His performance was a testament to his hard work and dedication throughout the season. The Brewers' decision to hold back pitcher Pat Murphy from bringing Misiorowski in to close out Game 4 proved wise, as it allowed the ace to conserve energy for Game 5. With the series already in their favor at 3-0, the team was able to rely on Misiorowski's fresh legs to secure the win. Misiorowski's workload this season has been carefully managed by the Brewers, who recognized his significant increase from last year's 141 ⅓ innings pitched to 193 ⅔. This deliberate approach allowed him to maintain a strong performance in Game 5 and ultimately contribute to the team's World Series victory. Misiorowski's impressive regular season campaign was marked by exceptional performance across various statistics. He led the majors in ERA and strikeouts, boasting a staggering 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts in 174 ⅔ innings of work. His dominance on the mound was further underscored by his league-leading WHIP, strikeout rate, and hit rate, showcasing his ability to limit walks and prevent hits. Misiorowski's sophomore season saw significant improvements from his rookie campaign, with a notable increase in his strikeout rate and decrease in his walk rate. Misiorowski's impressive sophomore season has set a high bar for future performance, and it's reasonable to expect even greater success in the years to come. A key factor in his continued growth will be building up stamina to maintain a strong level of play throughout the regular season. With consistent effort, he may be able to surpass 200 innings pitched next year, which would be an impressive achievement. The possibility of leading the Brewers to back-to-back championships and winning a second Cy Young Award is not far-fetched, given his exceptional talent and the team's recent success. Although his knees might not be as spry as they once were, Curry still managed to book it towards the rock and get into position for the play. However, his feet did touch the baseline, resulting in an out-of-bounds call. Despite this minor mishap, Curry quickly shook off the incident and continued to dominate the game. The Warriors' offense relied heavily on him to deliver against a Timberwolves team missing star player Anthony Edwards, but still boasting a formidable defense with long-armed defenders. Curry's clutch shooting helped his team stay ahead, particularly from the free throw line where he made all 16 of his attempts. As the night wore on, Curry's vintage performance became increasingly apparent, and it was clear that he remains one of the most potent forces in the league despite his advanced age. With 44 points under his belt, Curry had done just enough to secure a crucial win for the Warriors against a tough opponent. Jaden McDaniels was a constant thorn in Steph Curry's side throughout the game, using his 6-foot-9 frame to envelop him and make it difficult for him to get shots off. The Timberwolves forward has developed a reputation for being able to lock down scorers like Curry with his defensive skills. Despite McDaniels' best efforts, Curry was able to find openings on the court and capitalize on them. He pulled up from deep in transition early in the third quarter and hit a three-pointer with ease. The shot was a testament to his ability to make plays off the dribble and create scoring opportunities for himself. The first half of the game saw Curry go on a hot streak, hitting multiple three-pointers in quick succession. He began the stretch with a 3-pointer that curled off a screen, and followed it up with another from the top of the key just two possessions later. The Warriors' win was built on a strong foundation in the first half, but they faced tougher competition in the second. Minnesota's absence of star guard Edwards, who underwent arthroscopic surgery on his knee just two days prior, was a significant blow to their lineup. However, the Timberwolves still managed to put up a fierce fight, showcasing their resilience and determination. The Warriors' coaching staff, led by Steve Kerr, has been emphasizing the importance of understanding opposing teams' personnel this season. The Timberwolves' decision to let Jonathan Kuminga go after drafting him seventh overall in 2021 has clearly not been forgotten by Golden State's coaching staff. Despite being gone from Minnesota, Kuminga was still a focus for the Warriors before their game against the Timberwolves. Steve Kerr was asked about the contrast between Kuminga and Yaxel Lendeborg, who took his place as the team's top prospect this season. Kerr diplomatically highlighted the differences between these two players in a pregame press conference, acknowledging that they bring distinct qualities to the court. He praised their unique skills without comparing them directly. The emphasis on understanding the Timberwolves' personnel has been a key aspect of the Warriors' strategy all season, and their game plan against Minnesota reflects this focus. The Warriors' Kuminga was making waves in Minnesota by checking on Lendeborg, who has been heavily involved in the team's offense this season. This development came as a surprise to many, given that Kuminga had limited playing time with Golden State. In the first half, Kuminga made an immediate impact, sinking several three-pointers and a smooth elbow jumper for 12 points. His hot start helped the Warriors build a significant lead in the game. Minnesota, however, refused to back down. As the Timberwolves fought back, they began to find their rhythm from beyond the arc, with threes starting to fall regularly at Target Center. The crowd's energy picked up, and the home team started to chip away at the Warriors' lead. As the game intensified, a crucial block by De'Anthony Melton thwarted Dosunmu's attempt to narrow the gap, and McDaniels' two missed three-pointers added to the tension. The crowd's energy had already peaked, but Curry still managed to seal the win for Golden State with his impressive 44 points, securing a hard-fought victory. articles.title: Major leak of DHS employee records blocked by social media platform Bluesky
articles.summary: Bluesky has automatically blocked links to leaked records, labeling them as "malicious for safety reasons".
articles.content: A major leak of sensitive employee records belonging to the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has been blocked by social media platform Bluesky. The leak was published on Wednesday by the transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets. The leaked files include a wealth of personal information about DHS employees and contractors, including their names, contact details, and membership in internal groups tied to surveillance and undercover operations. This sensitive data appears to have been shared without authorization, violating Bluesky's community guidelines. Bluesky is automatically blocking links to the leaked records when users attempt to access them through its website or app, labeling them as "malicious for safety reasons. However, it remains unclear whether this block was imposed manually by the company or at the behest of a government agency. The Bluesky platform has been blocking links to a major leak of DHS employee records without warning users when they open these links through third-party apps like Klearsky. This move is particularly striking given Bluesky's stance on content moderation, which allows users to choose independent services that label or filter posts. The company promotes a decentralized approach to moderation, empowering users with more control over the content they see. Bluesky has come a long way since its inception as a Twitter research project in 2019. It gained independence and opened up to the public in February this year, and its mobile app has already attracted four million users in June. The company's open protocol allows outside developers to build their own Bluesky apps, which can choose from moderation labels offered by the company itself. This flexibility has raised questions about who or what is behind the block on DHS employee records links. The decision by tech platforms like Bluesky to block links to sensitive information raises questions about their role in censoring online content. According to experts, these companies often give in to government pressure, but ultimately cannot prevent the spread of information. In this case, Bluesky has blocked a website built by journalist maia arson crimew for searching through the leaked Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employee records. The site is part of a larger archive dubbed Icepick" made available by the group calling itself the Department of Peace to DDoSecrets and crimew. Meanwhile, X, a rival platform, has taken a different approach, directing users to the Icepick website through its Grok chatbot.
